dossier.architecture: Rear full-width acquisition, internally rigged elevator, pivoting arm and translating/rotating station forks.

subsystems.intake: Rear floor intake vectors cubes; compliant pivoting cone pickup reorients tipped cones for the gripper.
subsystems.transfer: Compliant cone handoff avoids adding an actively controlled orientation axis.
subsystems.scoring: Two-stage elevator with overextending carriage and internally routed Dyneema; pivoting arm carries the gripper.
subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve platform; exact module choice should be checked in released CAD.
subsystems.endgame: Spring-deployed forks translate and rotate through a cam/string arrangement, lifting the front before rotating the chassis.
subsystems.controls: AprilTag pose estimation from three cameras on an Orange Pi 5; retroreflective vision refines cone alignment and checks node occupancy.

versions: Angled-elevator alpha robot preceded later architecture.
Elevator gearing increased as placement-speed limits became clearer.
Interview also discusses later offseason vision changes; these are not labeled Championship configuration.
dossier.analysis: Useful for acquisition on the opposite side from scoring and for separating coarse localization from final-placement sensing. The compliant handoff is a geometric solution to an orientation problem.
limits: Interview was filmed after the main season; late-season versus offseason details require care.

context_documents.body:
# 2023-5940: Passive cone reorientation removes an axis only if the handoff remains tolerant

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A two-stage elevator has an overextending carriage and internally routed Dyneema. The rear collector vectors cubes and uses a compliant cone handoff to correct orientation before the scoring gripper receives it.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source links internal line routing to avoiding snags. The retained account describes passive cone reorientation in place of another controlled axis.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Moving orientation work into compliance reduces actuator/control count while making friction, piece pose and guide geometry decisive. Internal rigging protects lines but complicates inspection and replacement.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test extreme cone approaches, worn pieces and line service access; distinguish smooth demo transfer from statistical handoff reliability.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
